Here's how *advantage* and *disadvantage* work with attack modifier cards in **Gloomhaven (2nd Edition)**:

---

## Advantage

> With advantage, the attacker draws two modifiers and uses one of them. A monster always uses the better one, but a character may use either one.

---

## Disadvantage

> With disadvantage, the attacker draws two modifiers and always uses the worse one.

---

## Rolling Modifiers with Advantage/Disadvantage

This is where it gets more involved:

- **If the first draw is a *rolling modifier*:** Keep drawing additional modifiers one at a time until you draw a non-rolling modifier. Then draw **one more** card (ignoring any rolling icon on it). You now compare **the first non-rolling modifier** and that **final card**:
  - With *advantage*: Use all the initial rolling modifiers **plus** whichever of the last two you choose.
  - With *disadvantage*: **Ignore** all the initial rolling modifiers and use whichever of the last two is **worse**.

- **If the first draw is not a rolling modifier, but the second draw is:** The rolling icon on the second card is still **ignored**.

---

## Ambiguity & Special Cases

- When it's unclear which modifier is worse (e.g., non-numeric effects like elemental infusions or negative conditions), any non-numeric effect is considered to have a **positive but undefined value**, and the attacker **must use the one drawn first**.
- An attack **cannot** gain multiple instances of *advantage* or *disadvantage*. If an attack has **both**, they cancel out and it has **neither**.
- Any **ranged attack targeting an adjacent enemy** automatically gains *disadvantage*.

---

*(Source: Gloomhaven 2nd Edition Rulebook, pp. 24–25)*

- **Item #005**
- **Slot:** Head
- **Cost:** 10 gold

Here is a full summary of **Looting** in Gloomhaven (2nd Edition), based on the rulebook:

---

## Loot Ability (*Loot X*)

> "*Loot X* is an ability that allows a figure to loot all money tokens and treasure tiles within range X, including any in their current hex. This ability is unaffected by the presence of figures or overlay tiles. If there are no money tokens or treasure tiles within the specified range, the ability cannot be performed."

*(Rulebook, passage 63)*

---

## Money Tokens

- When a money token is looted, it is **removed from the map**.
- **If the looting figure is a monster**, nothing else happens.
- **If the looting figure is a character**, they place the token on their character mat.

---

## Treasure Tiles

- When a treasure tile is looted, it is **removed from the map**.
- **Monsters cannot loot treasure tiles.**
- If the looted treasure is a **numbered treasure**, reference its number in the Treasure Index and apply the effect.
- Only the looting character gains the reward — unless it is a random item design or random scenario.
- If a looting character gains a duplicate item they already own, they must **give it to another character or sell it immediately**.

*(Rulebook, passages 63–64)*

---

## End-of-Turn Looting

> "Characters must loot any money tokens or treasure tiles present in their hex at the end of their turn."

- **Only characters** perform end-of-turn looting. Monsters and summons do **not**.
- Note: characters loot the hex they occupy at the **end of their turn**, not at the end of each movement.

*(Rulebook, passages 76 & 137)*

**Yes, you can skip targets in a red hex AoE attack.**

The official FAQ states it directly:

> "Can I skip targets in a red hex AoE attack? Yes; a red hex AoE just determines the hexes where your **potential** targets are. Note - this is a change from the Gloomhaven 1e FAQ, and is to make it consistent with all other non-mandatory targeting."

*(Gloomhaven 2e FAQ, passage 31)*

So the red hex pattern defines **which figures you may target**, not which figures you **must** target. You can freely choose to leave some figures in the AoE unhit — just as you can with any other non-mandatory targeting in the game.

Here are the steps a character performs when taking a **long rest** in Gloomhaven (2nd Edition), per the Rulebook (p. 36):

**When to declare & perform it:**
- A long rest is **declared during the Card Selection step** (instead of playing two cards), provided the character has **at least two cards in their discard pile**.
- The long rest is performed on **initiative 99** and constitutes the character's **entire turn** for the round.

> *(Note: Per the FAQ, initiative 99 is not necessarily last — if a game effect pushes a figure's initiative above 99, it will act after your long rest. Your long rest is performed before monster turns on initiative 99.)*

---

**Steps performed when long resting (in order):**

1. **Lose one card of your choice** from your discard pile and **return the remaining cards to your hand**. *(This step is mandatory.)*

2. **Perform "*Heal* 2, self."** *(Optional.)*

3. **Recover all spent items.** *(Optional. Items can be used during the same turn in which they are recovered.)*

---

**Additional notes:**
- Cards **without lost icons** that are in your **active area** count as being in your discard pile for the purposes of whether you *can* long rest and what is eligible to lose — but they **do not** have to be returned to your hand when resting.

*Sources: Gloomhaven (2nd Edition) Rulebook, passages 77–78; GH2e FAQ.*

Here is what the Gloomhaven (2nd Edition) rulebook says about *Wound*:

> **Wound:** The figure suffers 1 damage at the start of each of their turns. Wound is removed when the figure is healed.

**Key interaction with *Heal*:**
A single *Heal* can remove both *Wound* and *Poison* from a figure at the same time. However, if *Poison* is also present, the hit point increase from the heal is prevented (the conditions are still removed).

**Source:** Gloomhaven (2nd Edition) Rulebook, passage 56–57.

In **Gloomhaven (2nd Edition)**, each character can bring a number of *Small* items (the small item slot) into a scenario equal to **half their character level, rounded up**.

> "Characters can each bring into a scenario a number of small items equal to half their level (rounded up)."

So the limit by level looks like this:

| 2 | 1 |
| 3 | 2 |
| 4 | 2 |
| 5 | 3 |
| 6 | 3 |
| 7 | 4 |
| 8 | 4 |
| 9 | 5 |

*(Source: Gloomhaven 2nd Edition Rulebook, p. 33 & Appendix C, p. 64)*

Here's how the recommended scenario level is calculated in **Gloomhaven (2nd Edition)**:

---

## Recommended Scenario Level

> The recommended scenario level is half the average character level (rounded up).

**Formula:** `Average Character Level ÷ 2 (rounded up)`

**Example:** If all characters are level 2, the average (2) ÷ 2 = 1, so the scenario is level 1. Only once a character reaches level 3 would the scenario level potentially increase to 2.

---

## Scenario Level Table

| Scenario Level | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monster Level | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
| Gold Conversion | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| Trap Damage | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| Hazardous Terrain | 1 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 4 |
| Bonus Experience | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 14 | 16 | 18 |

---

## Special Cases

- **The scenario level can always be set to any number from 0–7** at the start of a scenario, regardless of the recommendation.
- **Solo Mode:** Add 1 to the average character level *before* dividing by 2 and rounding up. For example, three level 4 characters in normal play gives scenario level 2, but in solo mode it becomes 3: `((4+4+4) ÷ 3 + 1) ÷ 2 = 3`.
- **Open Information variant:** Calculate scenario level the same way as solo mode (increased difficulty).

*(Gloomhaven 2nd Edition Rulebook, pp. 15 & 57)*

Here's what *Poison* does in **Gloomhaven (2nd Edition)**:

> **Poison:** All attacks targeting the figure gain "+1 Attack." Poison is removed when the figure is healed but, unlike *Wound*, poison prevents the heal from increasing the figure's current hit point value.

*(Gloomhaven 2e Rulebook, passage 56)*

### Key points to remember:

- *Poison* **buffs every attacker** targeting the afflicted figure — enemies and allies alike all gain +1 to their attack value against that figure.
- *Poison* is removed by a *Heal* effect, but **the hit point increase from that heal is prevented** — the heal only removes the condition, it does not restore any HP.
- A single *Heal* can remove both *Wound* and *Poison* simultaneously *(Rulebook, passage 57)*.
- *Poison* does **not** wear off on its own at the end of a turn — it persists until the figure is healed.

A *long rest* has an initiative value of **99**.

A few important clarifications from the official FAQ (Gloomhaven 2e FAQ, passage 35):

- It is **not** necessarily the last action of the round. If any game effect pushes a figure's initiative above 99, that figure will act **after** your long rest.
- Your long rest is performed **before** monster turns on initiative 99.
- It is **ambiguously timed** with other players also acting at initiative 99.

> *Source: Gloomhaven 2e Rulebook (passage 33) and official FAQ (passage 35)*
